Light-to-medium barrel char level.
Medium-heavy barrel char level, widely used for bourbon.

Traditional copper pot still used for Cognac's double distillation.
Italian bittersweet herbal liqueur.
US whiskey made from 100% malted barley at one distillery. The TTB recognized it as a formal category in 2024.
Brandy made in the US, mostly from grapes and largely in California.
Spirits and liqueurs flavored with anise or star anise; absinthe also contains wormwood.
Fruit raw materials for cider brandies such as Calvados and for pear eaux-de-vie.
Scandinavian spirit flavored mainly with caraway or dill.
Anise-flavored grape spirit of the Levant.
South and Southeast Asian spirits made from palm sap, sugarcane or rice; for example Batavia arrack and Sri Lankan coconut arrack.
Pressurized steam oven used by some tequila producers to cook agave quickly.
Okinawan distilled spirit made from long-grain rice with black koji (Aspergillus luchuensis).
Agave spirit from Sonora, Mexico, with its own denomination of origin.
Baijiu style with a clean, delicate profile, typified by Fenjiu.
Baijiu style made mainly from rice, with a soft profile, e.g. Guilin Sanhua.

A blend of malt (or pot still) whisky with grain whisky.
Blend of single malts from more than one distillery, with no grain whisky.
Cocktail of vodka, tomato juice and savory seasonings.

Spanish brandy aged in Sherry casks using the solera system in the Jerez area.
Brazilian cocktail of cachaça, lime and sugar.
Scotch whisky region on the Kintyre peninsula.

Sweet liqueur flavored with coffee, e.g. Kahlúa.
Casks that previously held Cognac, used to finish other spirits.
Gin styles where juniper is less dominant and other botanicals lead.

US whiskey from at least 80% corn. If aged, it must be in used or uncharred new oak.
Cocktail of vodka, orange liqueur, cranberry juice and lime.
Liqueur blended with dairy cream, e.g. Irish cream.
Rum with deep color from longer aging, added caramel or molasses.

Machine that extracts sugars from raw agave with water and pressure, sometimes with acid.
Secondary pot vessel in American distilling that redistills the spirit vapor from the first still.
Cocktail of gin (or vodka) and dry vermouth.
Leftover liquid from previous distillations, used in Jamaican rum production to build heavy flavor.
Traditional low, earth-floored warehouse with casks stacked a few high.

Clear fruit brandy, e.g. Kirsch (cherry) or Poire Williams (pear).
Cocktail of vodka, espresso and coffee liqueur.
Used bourbon barrels, the most common cask for maturing Scotch.
Goan spirit made from cashew apple or coconut palm sap.
Casks seasoned with dry Sherry, used to finish spirits.
Vodka with added natural or artificial flavors.
Mash bill using corn, rye, wheat and malted barley.
Cocktail of gin, lemon, sugar and Champagne.
Sweetened spirit flavored with fruit, e.g. lemon zest or blackcurrant.
Lightly aged or colored rum, between white and dark.
Whisky made from grains other than, or in addition to, malted barley, usually in column stills.
Vodka distilled from cereals such as wheat or rye.
Vodka distilled from grapes.
Raw material for brandies such as Cognac, Armagnac and pisco.
Italian spirit distilled from grape pomace.
Liqueurs flavored with many herbs, historically made by monks.
Bourbon with a relatively high share of rye in its mash bill, giving spicier flavor.
The largest Scotch whisky region by area.
Pot still with an attached rectifying column, able to make different spirit styles.
Malt whisky made in India, where warm climates speed up maturation.
Scotch whiskies from the islands other than Islay (e.g. Skye, Orkney, Mull, Jura, Arran), grouped under the Highland region.
Scotch whisky region on the island of Islay, known for peated malts.
Jamaican rum made in pot stills, often very high in esters.
Agave harvest by jimadores, who cut leaves off the agave heart with a sharp tool called a coa.
Unaged or lightly aged, often filtered, clear rum.
Scotch whisky region in southern Scotland, historically triple-distilled.
Casks that previously held Madeira wine, used to finish spirits.
Tiki cocktail of rum, lime, orange curaçao and orgeat.
Barley that has been germinated and dried; the base of malt whisky.
Cocktail of gin, sweet vermouth, maraschino and bitters, a predecessor of the Martini.
Above-ground masonry oven used to steam-cook agave for tequila.
Mexican agave spirit regulated by NOM-070, with classes by aging.
Drink of sparkling wine and orange juice.
Sugar-refining by-product and the base of most rum.
Cocktail of vodka, ginger beer and lime.
Modern cocktail of mezcal, Yellow Chartreuse, Aperol and lime in equal parts.
Gin or rum bottled at about 57% ABV (100 UK proof).
Alcohol-free drinks that imitate bitter aperitifs.
Alcohol-free botanical distillates or infusions in a gin style.
Alcohol-free drinks imitating whiskey flavors.
Whisky bottled without chill filtration, keeping more texture.
Liqueurs flavored with nuts or apricot kernels.
Lightly sweetened historical gin style.
Casks seasoned with oxidatively aged Oloroso Sherry, used for maturation or finishing.
Fermenting in open vats, exposed to air and wild microbes, versus closed tanks.
Orange-peel flavored liqueurs.
Spirit bottled well above standard strength.
Warehouse where casks are stored upright on pallets.
Modern cocktail of bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino and lemon in equal parts.
Casks seasoned with sweet PX Sherry, used for finishing.
Modern cocktail of blended Scotch, lemon, honey-ginger syrup and a float of peated Scotch.
Cocktail of rum, pineapple and coconut cream.
Gin made in Plymouth, England; it formerly had its own geographical indication.
Casks that previously held Port wine, used to finish spirits.
Vodka distilled from potatoes.
Raw material for some vodkas and aquavits.
US proof is twice the ABV (100 proof = 50% ABV).
Adding water to bring spirit down to bottling strength.
Hungarian fruit brandy with protected status.
Agave spirit from Jalisco, Mexico, with its own denomination of origin.
Turkish anise-flavored grape spirit.
Casks that previously held red wine, used to finish spirits.
Vapor that condenses and falls back in a still; more reflux gives a lighter, purer spirit.
Raw material for shochu, awamori and some baijiu.
Multi-story warehouse with barrels on wooden racks, typical for bourbon.
Mill that crushes malt or grain between rollers.
Casks that previously held rum, used to finish other spirits.
Spicy grain used in rye whiskey and bourbon mash bills.
US whiskey made from at least 51% rye and aged in new charred oak.
New Orleans cocktail of rye or Cognac, sugar, Peychaud's bitters and an absinthe rinse.

Japanese single-distilled spirit from ingredients such as barley, sweet potato or rice.
Drinks made with shrub, a vinegar-based fruit syrup.

Bolivian grape brandy made from Muscat of Alexandria.
Grain whisky from a single distillery.
Irish whiskey from malted and unmalted barley, distilled in pot stills at one distillery.
Whisky made from 100% malted barley at one distillery.
Plum brandy of Central and Eastern Europe.
Gin-based liqueur flavored with sloe berries.
Korean distilled spirit, traditionally from rice; mass-market versions are diluted and sweetened.

Spirit from the desert spoon plant (Dasylirion) of northern Mexico.
Scotch whisky region along the River Spey, with the most distilleries.
Rum flavored with spices such as vanilla and cinnamon.
Venetian drink of Prosecco, a bitter aperitif and soda water.
Fresh cane juice, the base of rhum agricole and cachaça.
Mash started fresh, without backset from a previous distillation.
Malt whisky made in Taiwan, matured quickly in a subtropical climate.
Barrel heat treatment that toasts the wood first and then chars it.
Margarita variation with agave syrup instead of orange liqueur.
Distilling three times, traditional in much Irish whiskey and in some Lowland Scotch.
Aging in hot climates, where faster evaporation and wood interaction speed up maturation.
Mixed drinks made without alcohol.
Fermented liquid that goes into the still.
Whisky distilled in Wales.
Grain used in wheated bourbon, wheat whiskey and many vodkas.
US whiskey made from at least 51% wheat.
Bourbon that uses wheat instead of rye as its secondary grain.
Cocktail of whiskey, lemon, sugar and optionally egg white.
